## Où j'en suis
Idempotency-Key support on POST /v1/refunds is built on a Postgres store with a 72h TTL, a 409 on in-flight retries and canonical JSON hashing. Tomer's review comments are addressed and the docs are updated. The facts show PR quillon/core#1437 as merged, even though the agent's last messages still described it as awaiting re-review. The read-only SQL listing the 14 Pinecrest duplicates is done (about $3,212.40 gross), and its CSV is saved but not committed.

- [en-cours] Pinecrest duplicate list: the CSV is generated but net amounts are not final.
- [prochaine-étape] Check net amounts with Marcus (2 duplicates were partially reversed by support).
- [prochaine-étape] Send the corrected list to Carla by Friday, before Pinecrest's weekend payout reconciliation.
- [essai-raté] Redis store failed with CROSSSLOT in cluster mode, and Redis is flushed on failover, so replays could double-refund.
- [décision] Use Postgres with a unique index on (merchant_id, idempotency_key) instead of Redis. (source: t05)
- [décision] Retain keys for 72h, not 24h. (source: t09)
- [décision] No script touches money: no automatic reversal backfill, only a read-only SQL listing. (source: t19)
